# Brings an account archive (made by Account::Export) back in as a brand new account.
#
# Records are restored in the order the archive lists them, straight into the database in batches.
# The account has no members until the very end, so nobody can see a half-restored account. If anything
# goes wrong, every row and file created for it is removed (see Account::DataTransfer::Purge), so a failed
# import leaves nothing behind.
class Account::Import < ApplicationRecord
  STALE_AFTER = 1.day
  INVALID_ARCHIVE_MESSAGE = "This file isn't a Fizzy account export we can import.".freeze
  UNEXPECTED_ERROR_MESSAGE = "Something went wrong while importing the account. Please try again, or contact support@fizzy.do if it keeps happening.".freeze

  belongs_to :identity

  enum :status, { pending: "pending", processing: "processing", completed: "completed", failed: "failed" }

  scope :stale, -> { processing.where(updated_at: ..STALE_AFTER.ago) }

  class << self
    def create_from_upload!(identity:, file:)
      service = ActiveStorage::Blob.service
      key = ActiveStorage::Blob.generate_unique_secure_token(length: 28)

      service.upload(key, file.tempfile)

      create!(
        identity: identity,
        filename: file.original_filename,
        byte_size: file.size,
        storage_service: service.name,
        storage_key: key
      )
    end

    def cleanup_stale
      stale.find_each do |import|
        import.fail_with("The import stopped before it finished. Please try again.")
      end
    end
  end

  def process_later
    Account::Import::ProcessJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def process_now
    discard_partial_account
    processing!

    @people = []
    read_archive
    finish_account

    completed!
    ImportMailer.completed(self).deliver_later
  rescue ZipFile::InvalidArchive, ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    fail_with(error.message)
  rescue StandardError => error
    Rails.error.report(error, handled: true, severity: :error)
    fail_with(UNEXPECTED_ERROR_MESSAGE)
  ensure
    delete_upload
  end

  def fail_with(message)
    discard_partial_account
    update!(status: :failed, error_message: message)
    ImportMailer.failed(self).deliver_later
  ensure
    delete_upload if stale_cleanup?
  end

  # Used by the record sets while restoring. The seed is this import's own ID, so
  # IDs from the archive never collide with records that already exist.
  def identifiers
    @identifiers ||= Account::DataTransfer::IdentifierMap.new(id)
  end

  def create_account(row)
    @account = Account.create!(
      id: identifiers.map(row["id"]),
      name: row["name"],
      cards_count: row["cards_count"] || 0,
      created_at: row["created_at"],
      updated_at: row["updated_at"]
    )

    # Account creation gives every account a default auto-close period; the archive has the real one.
    @account.entropy&.delete
    update!(account_id: @account.id)
    @account
  end

  def add_person(row, identity_email)
    @people << [ row, identity_email ]
  end

  private
    def read_archive
      manifest_read = false

      ZipFile::Reader.new(archive_input).each_entry do |entry|
        if entry.name == "manifest.json"
          read_manifest(entry)
          manifest_read = true
        elsif !manifest_read
          raise ZipFile::InvalidArchive, INVALID_ARCHIVE_MESSAGE
        elsif entry.name.start_with?(Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::FileRecordSet::PATH_PREFIX)
          require_account!
          file_record_set.read_from(entry, self)
        elsif (record_set = record_sets_by_path[entry.name])
          require_account! unless record_set.is_a?(Account::DataTransfer::AccountRecordSet)
          record_set.read_from(entry, self)
        else
          entry.skip
        end
      end

      require_account!
    end

    def read_manifest(entry)
      manifest = JSON.parse(entry.read.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8))

      unless manifest["format"] == Account::DataTransfer::Manifest::FORMAT
        raise ZipFile::InvalidArchive, INVALID_ARCHIVE_MESSAGE
      end

      if manifest["version"].to_i > Account::DataTransfer::Manifest::VERSION
        raise ZipFile::InvalidArchive, "This account was exported from a newer version of Fizzy. Please update this instance and try again."
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError
      raise ZipFile::InvalidArchive, INVALID_ARCHIVE_MESSAGE
    end

    def require_account!
      raise ZipFile::InvalidArchive, "The archive is missing its account record" unless @account
    end

    def record_sets
      @record_sets ||= Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new(nil).record_sets
    end

    def record_sets_by_path
      @record_sets_by_path ||= record_sets.index_by(&:path)
    end

    def file_record_set
      @file_record_set ||= record_sets.find { |record_set| record_set.is_a?(Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::FileRecordSet) }
    end

    # Once all the records are in, the people come in as well, so the account only becomes reachable at this point.
    def finish_account
      Current.with_account(@account) do
        ApplicationRecord.transaction do
          restore_people
          @account.reconcile_storage
        end

        reindex_search
      end
    end

    def restore_people
      rows = @people.map do |row, identity_email|
        person_identity = identity_email.present? ? Identity.find_or_create_by!(email_address: identity_email) : nil
        row.merge(
          "identity_id" => person_identity&.id,
          "verified_at" => nil
        ).tap do |person|
          if person_identity && person_identity == identity
            person["role"] = "owner"
            person["verified_at"] = Time.current
            @importer_restored = true
          end
        end
      end

      User.insert_all(rows) if rows.any?

      @account.users.create!(identity: identity, name: importer_name, role: :owner, verified_at: Time.current) unless @importer_restored
      @account.users.find_by(role: :system) || @account.users.create!(role: :system, name: "System")
    end

    def importer_name
      identity.users.where.not(account_id: @account.id).order(:created_at).last&.name ||
        identity.email_address.split("@").first
    end

    def reindex_search
      Card.where(account: @account).published.includes(:rich_text_description).find_each(&:reindex)
      Comment.where(account: @account).includes(:rich_text_body, :card).find_each(&:reindex)
    end

    def discard_partial_account
      return if account_id.blank?

      Account::DataTransfer::Purge.new(account_id).call
      update!(account_id: nil)
    end

    def archive_input
      ZipFile::ChunkedInput.new { |&block| archive_service.download(storage_key, &block) }
    end

    def archive_service
      ActiveStorage::Blob.services.fetch(storage_service)
    end

    def delete_upload
      archive_service.delete(storage_key)
    rescue StandardError => error
      Rails.error.report(error, handled: true, severity: :warning)
    end

    def stale_cleanup?
      false
    end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class ZipFile::ReaderTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "archive", ".zip" ])
    @tempfile.binmode
    @writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(@tempfile)
  end

  teardown do
    @tempfile.close!
  end

  test "reads back every entry written by the writer, in order" do
    @writer.add_file("manifest.json", '{"format":"x"}')
    @writer.add_file("records/cards.ndjson") { |sink| 3.times { |i| sink.write("{\"n\":#{i}}\n") } }
    @writer.add_file("empty.txt", "")
    finish_archive

    entries = read_entries(archive_bytes)

    assert_equal [ "manifest.json", "records/cards.ndjson", "empty.txt" ], entries.keys
    assert_equal '{"format":"x"}', entries["manifest.json"]
    assert_equal "{\"n\":0}\n{\"n\":1}\n{\"n\":2}\n", entries["records/cards.ndjson"]
    assert_equal "", entries["empty.txt"]
  end

  test "reads archives delivered in chunks of any size" do
    @writer.add_file("big.bin") { |sink| 3.times { sink.write(Random.bytes(200_000)) } }
    @writer.add_file("text.txt", "héllo wörld")
    finish_archive

    [ 1, 7, 4096, 1.megabyte ].each do |chunk_size|
      entries = read_entries(archive_bytes, chunk_size: chunk_size)

      assert_equal 600_000, entries["big.bin"].bytesize, "chunk size #{chunk_size}"
      assert_equal "héllo wörld", entries["text.txt"], "chunk size #{chunk_size}"
    end
  end

  test "yields each line of an entry, even when lines span chunks" do
    lines = (1..500).map { |i| "{\"id\":#{i},\"title\":\"#{"x" * i}\"}" }
    @writer.add_file("records/cards.ndjson", lines.join("\n") + "\n")
    finish_archive

    read_lines = []
    ZipFile::Reader.new(chunked(archive_bytes, 333)).each_entry do |entry|
      entry.each_line { |line| read_lines << line }
    end

    assert_equal lines, read_lines
  end

  test "skipping an entry moves on to the next one" do
    @writer.add_file("first.txt") { |sink| sink.write("a" * 100_000) }
    @writer.add_file("second.txt", "second")
    finish_archive

    names = []
    ZipFile::Reader.new(chunked(archive_bytes, 1000)).each_entry do |entry|
      names << entry.name
      entry.skip
    end

    assert_equal [ "first.txt", "second.txt" ], names
  end

  test "reports the decompressed size of an entry once read" do
    @writer.add_file("data.bin", "x" * 12_345)
    finish_archive

    ZipFile::Reader.new(chunked(archive_bytes, 64)).each_entry do |entry|
      entry.read
      assert_equal 12_345, entry.decompressed_size
    end
  end

  test "rejects data that is not a zip archive" do
    error = assert_raises ZipFile::InvalidArchive do
      read_entries("this is definitely not a zip file")
    end

    assert_match "isn't a valid ZIP archive", error.message
  end

  test "rejects an archive that is cut off" do
    @writer.add_file("records/accounts.ndjson", "a" * 50_000)
    @writer.add_file("records/users.ndjson", "b" * 50_000)
    finish_archive

    truncated = archive_bytes.byteslice(0, archive_bytes.bytesize / 2)

    assert_raises ZipFile::InvalidArchive do
      read_entries(truncated)
    end
  end

  test "rejects damaged entry data" do
    @writer.add_file("records/cards.ndjson", "{\"title\":\"hello\"}\n" * 500)
    finish_archive

    damaged = archive_bytes.dup
    damaged.setbyte(200, damaged.getbyte(200) ^ 0x5A)

    error = assert_raises ZipFile::InvalidArchive do
      read_entries(damaged)
    end

    assert_match "damaged", error.message
  end

  private
    def finish_archive
      @writer.close
      @tempfile.flush
    end

    def archive_bytes
      File.binread(@tempfile.path)
    end

    def chunked(bytes, size)
      pieces = bytes.bytes.each_slice(size).map { |slice| slice.pack("C*") }
      ZipFile::ChunkedInput.new { |&block| pieces.each(&block) }
    end

    def read_entries(bytes, chunk_size: 64.kilobytes)
      entries = {}

      ZipFile::Reader.new(chunked(bytes, chunk_size)).each_entry do |entry|
        entries[entry.name] = entry.read.to_s.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
      end

      entries
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class ZipFile::WriterTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "tracks the size and checksum of what it writes" do
    tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "writer", ".zip" ])
    tempfile.binmode

    writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(tempfile)
    writer.add_file("hello.txt", "Hello, World!")
    writer.add_file("numbers.txt") { |sink| 1000.times { |i| sink.write("#{i}\n") } }
    writer.close
    tempfile.flush

    assert_equal File.size(tempfile.path), writer.byte_size
    assert_equal Base64.strict_encode64(Digest::MD5.file(tempfile.path).digest), writer.checksum
  ensure
    tempfile&.close!
  end

  test "lists the entries it has written" do
    writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(StringIO.new.binmode)
    writer.add_file("docs/readme.txt", "Readme")
    writer.add_file("docs/guide.txt", "Guide")
    writer.add_file("images/logo.png", "PNG data")
    writer.close

    assert writer.exists?("docs/readme.txt")
    assert_not writer.exists?("missing.txt")
    assert_equal [ "docs/guide.txt", "docs/readme.txt" ], writer.glob("docs/*.txt")
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class Account::DataTransfer::IdentifierMapTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @seed = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
    @map = Account::DataTransfer::IdentifierMap.new(@seed)
    @exported_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
  end

  test "maps an exported ID to the same new ID every time, for one import" do
    assert_equal @map.map(@exported_id), @map.map(@exported_id)
  end

  test "maps the same exported ID differently for a different import" do
    other = Account::DataTransfer::IdentifierMap.new(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate)

    assert_not_equal @map.map(@exported_id), other.map(@exported_id)
  end

  test "produces IDs in the same shape as the rest of the app" do
    mapped = @map.map(@exported_id)

    assert_equal ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid::BASE36_LENGTH, mapped.length
    assert_not_equal @exported_id, mapped
  end

  test "re-signs a signed global ID so it points at the mapped record" do
    user = users(:david)
    sgid = user.attachable_sgid

    mapped_sgid = @map.map_sgid(sgid)
    located = GlobalID::Locator.locate_signed(mapped_sgid, for: ActionText::Attachable::LOCATOR_NAME)

    assert_not_nil mapped_sgid
    assert_not_equal sgid, mapped_sgid
    assert_equal @map.map(user.id), located.id if located
    assert_equal "User", GlobalID.parse(SignedGlobalID.parse(mapped_sgid, for: ActionText::Attachable::LOCATOR_NAME).to_s).model_name
  end

  test "returns nil for references it can't understand" do
    assert_nil @map.map_sgid("not-an-sgid")
    assert_nil @map.map_sgid("eyJhIjoxfQ==--deadbeef")
  end
end

module DataTransferTestHelper
  # Runs a real account export and returns the archive as a rewound tempfile.
  def export_account_to_file(account = accounts("37s"), user: users(:jason))
    export = Account::Export.create!(user: user, account: account)
    export.process_now
    assert export.completed?, "Export should complete, but was #{export.status}"

    download_to_file(export)
  end

  def export_cards_to_file(user)
    export = User::Export.create!(user: user, account: user.account)
    export.process_now
    assert export.completed?, "Export should complete, but was #{export.status}"

    download_to_file(export)
  end

  def download_to_file(export)
    tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "archive", ".zip" ])
    tempfile.binmode
    export.file.download { |chunk| tempfile.write(chunk) }
    tempfile.flush
    tempfile.rewind
    tempfile
  end

  # Stores the archive the way the upload form does, and returns the import that was created for it.
  def upload_import(archive, identity: identities(:kevin), filename: "export.zip")
    upload = ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile.new(tempfile: archive, filename: filename, type: "application/zip")
    Account::Import.create_from_upload!(identity: identity, file: upload)
  end

  def import_archive(archive, identity: identities(:kevin))
    upload_import(archive, identity: identity).tap(&:process_now).reload
  end

  def new_account_from(import)
    import.account || flunk("Import should have created an account, but it's #{import.status}: #{import.error_message}")
  end

  def archive_entries(archive)
    names = []
    ZipFile::Reader.new(File.open(archive.path, "rb")).each_entry do |entry|
      names << entry.name
      entry.skip
    end
    names
  end

  def read_archive_entry(archive, wanted)
    content = nil
    ZipFile::Reader.new(File.open(archive.path, "rb")).each_entry do |entry|
      if entry.name == wanted
        content = entry.read.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
      else
        entry.skip
      end
    end
    content
  end

  def storage_file_count
    Dir.glob(File.join(ActiveStorage::Blob.service.root, "**", "*")).count { |path| File.file?(path) }
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class Account::ExportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include DataTransferTestHelper

  setup do
    @account = accounts("37s")
    @user = users(:jason)
  end

  test "creates an archive of the whole account and marks it ready for a day" do
    export = Account::Export.create!(user: @user, account: @account)

    freeze_time do
      export.process_now

      assert export.completed?
      assert export.file.attached?
      assert_equal Time.current, export.completed_at
      assert_equal 1.day.from_now, export.expires_at
      assert export.downloadable?
    end
  end

  test "the archive starts with a manifest and contains every table of the account" do
    archive = export_account_to_file(@account)
    entries = archive_entries(archive)

    assert_equal "manifest.json", entries.first
    assert_includes entries, "records/cards.ndjson"
    assert_includes entries, "records/comments.ndjson"
    assert_includes entries, "records/boards.ndjson"
    assert_includes entries, "records/users.ndjson"
    assert_includes entries.select { it.start_with?("records/") }.index("records/accounts.ndjson").to_s, "0"
  end

  test "the manifest identifies the archive format" do
    manifest = JSON.parse(read_archive_entry(export_account_to_file(@account), "manifest.json"))

    assert_equal Account::DataTransfer::Manifest::FORMAT, manifest["format"]
    assert_equal Account::DataTransfer::Manifest::VERSION, manifest["version"]
    assert_equal @account.name, manifest["account_name"]
  end

  test "the archive doesn't contain the export files themselves" do
    export_account_to_file(@account)
    archive = export_account_to_file(@account)

    assert_no_match(/export/i, archive_entries(archive).grep(%r{\Afiles/}).join)
    assert_empty archive_entries(archive).grep(%r{\Afiles/}).select { |path| path.include?(".zip") }
  end

  test "includes the files attached to cards and comments, byte for byte" do
    card = cards(:logo)
    card.image.attach io: StringIO.new("picture bytes"), filename: "logo.png", content_type: "image/png"
    blob = card.image.blob

    archive = export_account_to_file(@account)

    assert_includes archive_entries(archive), "files/#{blob.id}/logo.png"
    assert_equal "picture bytes", read_archive_entry(archive, "files/#{blob.id}/logo.png")
  end

  test "emails the person who asked, with a link to the download" do
    export = Account::Export.create!(user: @user, account: @account)

    assert_enqueued_emails 1 do
      export.process_now
    end

    email = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    assert_equal [ @user.identity.email_address ], email.to
    assert_match "is ready", email.subject
    assert_match "/exports/#{export.id}", email.html_part.body.to_s
  end

  test "a failed export is marked as failed and the person is told" do
    export = Account::Export.create!(user: @user, account: @account)
    Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.any_instance.stubs(:write_to).raises(StandardError, "disk full")

    assert_enqueued_emails 1 do
      export.process_now
    end

    assert export.failed?
    assert_not export.file.attached?
    assert_not export.downloadable?
    assert_match "couldn't be created", ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last.subject
  end

  test "only the person who asked can download the export" do
    export = export_for(@account)

    assert export.accessible_to?(@user)
    assert_not export.accessible_to?(users(:kevin))
  end

  test "an expired export can't be downloaded" do
    export = export_for(@account)
    export.update!(expires_at: 1.minute.ago)

    assert_not export.downloadable?
    assert_not export.accessible_to?(@user)
  end

  test "cleanup removes expired exports and their files" do
    export = export_for(@account)
    export.update!(expires_at: 1.minute.ago)
    fresh = export_for(@account)

    Export.cleanup

    assert_not Export.exists?(export.id)
    assert Export.exists?(fresh.id)
  end

  private
    def export_for(account)
      Account::Export.create!(user: users(:jason), account: account).tap(&:process_now)
    end
end

class Account::DataTransfer::ActionText::RichTextRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  ATTACHMENT_TAG = /<action-text-attachment\b[^>]*>/
  SGID_ATTRIBUTE = /\ssgid="([^"]*)"/

  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::ActionText::RichText)
  end

  private
    def records
      ::ActionText::RichText.where(account: account)
    end

    # The body is typed as rendered content, which wraps it in markup and rewrites attachments on the way out.
    # Export the stored text exactly as it is, so importing it again doesn't change it.
    def serialize(record)
      super.merge("body" => record.read_attribute_before_type_cast("body"))
    end

    def import_row(data, import)
      super.tap do |row|
        row["body"] = remap_attachment_references(row["body"], import) if row["body"]
      end
    end

    # Attachments and mentions in a body are referenced by signed global IDs. Each one is re-pointed at
    # the imported record and re-signed. A reference we can't follow is dropped, so it never points at
    # a record that belongs to some other account.
    def remap_attachment_references(body, import)
      body.gsub(ATTACHMENT_TAG) do |tag|
        tag.sub(SGID_ATTRIBUTE) do
          sgid = import.identifiers.map_sgid(Regexp.last_match(1))
          sgid ? %( sgid="#{sgid}") : ""
        end
      end
    end
end
RUBYEOF

require "test_helper"

class ZipFile::S3Test < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include DataTransferTestHelper

  setup do
    @s3 = ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service.new(bucket: "fizzy-test", region: "us-east-1", access_key_id: "test", secret_access_key: "test")
    ActiveStorage::Blob.services.stubs(:fetch).with(ActiveStorage::Blob.service.name).returns(@s3)
  end

  test "an archive is streamed to S3 and recorded with its size and checksum" do
    uploaded = StringIO.new.binmode
    @s3.stubs(:upload_stream).yields(uploaded)
    export = Account::Export.create!(user: users(:jason), account: accounts("37s"))

    ZipFile.create_for(export.file, filename: "export.zip") do |zip|
      zip.add_file("hello.txt", "hello from S3")
    end

    blob = export.file.blob
    assert_equal uploaded.string.bytesize, blob.byte_size
    assert_equal Base64.strict_encode64(Digest::MD5.digest(uploaded.string)), blob.checksum

    entries = {}
    ZipFile::Reader.new(StringIO.new(uploaded.string)).each_entry { |entry| entries[entry.name] = entry.read }
    assert_equal({ "hello.txt" => "hello from S3" }, entries)
  end

class ZipFile::S3Test < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include DataTransferTestHelper

  setup do
    @s3 = ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service.new(bucket: "fizzy-test", region: "us-east-1", access_key_id: "test", secret_access_key: "test")
  end

  test "an archive is streamed to S3 and recorded with its size and checksum" do

    use_s3 do

      @s3.stubs(:download_chunk).returns("")

        zip.add_file("hello.txt", "hello from S3")
      end
    end

    blob = export.file.blob
    assert_equal uploaded.string.bytesize, blob.byte_size
    assert_equal Base64.strict_encode64(Digest::MD5.digest(uploaded.string)), blob.checksum

    entries = {}
    ZipFile::Reader.new(StringIO.new(uploaded.string)).each_entry { |entry| entries[entry.name] = entry.read }
    assert_equal({ "hello.txt" => "hello from S3" }, entries)
  end

  test "an import reads its archive from S3 and uploads each file with its checksum" do
    picture = "a picture on its way to S3"

      import.process_now

  private
    def use_s3(&block)
      ActiveStorage::Blob.services.stubs(:fetch).returns(@s3)

    ensure

    end
end

# Brings an account archive (made by Account::Export) back in as a brand new account.
#
# Records are restored in the order the archive lists them, straight into the database in batches.
# The account has no members until the very end, so nobody can see a half-restored account. If anything
# goes wrong, every row and file created for it is removed (see Account::DataTransfer::Purge), so a failed
# import leaves nothing behind.
class Account::Import < ApplicationRecord
  STALE_AFTER = 1.day
  INVALID_ARCHIVE_MESSAGE = "This file isn't a Fizzy account export we can import.".freeze
  UNEXPECTED_ERROR_MESSAGE = "Something went wrong while importing the account. Please try again, or contact support@fizzy.do if it keeps happening.".freeze

  belongs_to :identity

  enum :status, { pending: "pending", processing: "processing", completed: "completed", failed: "failed" }

  scope :stale, -> { processing.where(updated_at: ..STALE_AFTER.ago) }

  class << self
    def create_from_upload!(identity:, file:)
      service = ActiveStorage::Blob.service
      key = ActiveStorage::Blob.generate_unique_secure_token(length: 28)

      service.upload(key, file.tempfile)

      create!(
        identity: identity,
        filename: file.original_filename,
        byte_size: file.size,
        storage_service: service.name,
        storage_key: key
      )
    end

    def cleanup_stale
      stale.find_each do |import|
        import.fail_with("The import stopped before it finished. Please try again.")
        import.delete_upload
      end
    end
  end

  def account
    Account.find_by(id: account_id) if account_id
  end

  def process_later
    Account::Import::ProcessJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def process_now
    discard_partial_account
    processing!

    @people = []
    read_archive
    finish_account

    completed!
    ImportMailer.completed(self).deliver_later
  rescue ZipFile::InvalidArchive, ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    fail_with(error.message)
  rescue StandardError => error
    Rails.error.report(error, handled: true, severity: :error)
    fail_with(UNEXPECTED_ERROR_MESSAGE)
  ensure
    delete_upload
  end

  def fail_with(message)
    discard_partial_account
    update!(status: :failed, error_message: message)
    ImportMailer.failed(self).deliver_later
  end

  def delete_upload
    archive_service.delete(storage_key)
  rescue StandardError => error
    Rails.error.report(error, handled: true, severity: :warning)
  end

  # Used by the record sets while restoring. The seed is this import's own ID, so
  # IDs from the archive never collide with records that already exist.
  def identifiers
    @identifiers ||= Account::DataTransfer::IdentifierMap.new(id)
  end

  def create_account(row)
    @account = Account.create!(
      id: row["id"],
      name: row["name"],
      cards_count: row["cards_count"] || 0,
      created_at: row["created_at"],
      updated_at: row["updated_at"]
    )

    # Account creation gives every account a default auto-close period; the archive has the real one.
    @account.entropy&.delete
    update!(account_id: @account.id)
    @account
  end

  def add_person(row, identity_email)
    @people << [ row, identity_email ]
  end

  private
    def read_archive
      manifest_read = false

      ZipFile::Reader.new(archive_input).each_entry do |entry|
        if entry.name == "manifest.json"
          read_manifest(entry)
          manifest_read = true
        elsif !manifest_read
          raise ZipFile::InvalidArchive, INVALID_ARCHIVE_MESSAGE
        elsif entry.name.start_with?(Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::FileRecordSet::PATH_PREFIX)
          require_account!
          file_record_set.read_from(entry, self)
        elsif (record_set = record_sets_by_path[entry.name])
          require_account! unless record_set.is_a?(Account::DataTransfer::AccountRecordSet)
          record_set.read_from(entry, self)
        else
          entry.skip
        end
      end

      require_account!
    end

    def read_manifest(entry)
      manifest = JSON.parse(entry.read.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8))

      unless manifest["format"] == Account::DataTransfer::Manifest::FORMAT
        raise ZipFile::InvalidArchive, INVALID_ARCHIVE_MESSAGE
      end

      if manifest["version"].to_i > Account::DataTransfer::Manifest::VERSION
        raise ZipFile::InvalidArchive, "This account was exported from a newer version of Fizzy. Please update this instance and try again."
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError
      raise ZipFile::InvalidArchive, INVALID_ARCHIVE_MESSAGE
    end

    def require_account!
      raise ZipFile::InvalidArchive, "The archive is missing its account record" unless @account
    end

    def record_sets
      @record_sets ||= Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new(nil).record_sets
    end

    def record_sets_by_path
      @record_sets_by_path ||= record_sets.index_by(&:path)
    end

    def file_record_set
      @file_record_set ||= record_sets.find { |record_set| record_set.is_a?(Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::FileRecordSet) }
    end

    # Once all the records are in, the people come in as well, so the account only becomes reachable at this point.
    def finish_account
      Current.with_account(@account) do
        ApplicationRecord.transaction do
          restore_people
          @account.reconcile_storage
        end

        reindex_search
      end
    end

    def restore_people
      rows = @people.map do |row, identity_email|
        person_identity = identity_email.present? ? Identity.find_or_create_by!(email_address: identity_email) : nil
        row.merge(
          "identity_id" => person_identity&.id,
          "verified_at" => nil
        ).tap do |person|
          if person_identity && person_identity == identity
            person["role"] = "owner"
            person["verified_at"] = Time.current
            @importer_restored = true
          end
        end
      end

      User.insert_all(rows) if rows.any?

      @account.users.create!(identity: identity, name: importer_name, role: :owner, verified_at: Time.current) unless @importer_restored
      @account.users.find_by(role: :system) || @account.users.create!(role: :system, name: "System")
    end

    def importer_name
      identity.users.where.not(account_id: @account.id).order(:created_at).last&.name ||
        identity.email_address.split("@").first
    end

    def reindex_search
      Card.where(account: @account).published.includes(:rich_text_description).find_each(&:reindex)
      Comment.where(account: @account).includes(:rich_text_body, :card).find_each(&:reindex)
    end

    def discard_partial_account
      return if account_id.blank?

      Account::DataTransfer::Purge.new(account_id).call
      update!(account_id: nil)
    end

    def archive_input
      ZipFile::ChunkedInput.new { |&block| archive_service.download(storage_key, &block) }
    end

    def archive_service
      ActiveStorage::Blob.services.fetch(storage_service)
    end
end

    # Gives an entry the size its record declares, and refuses to read past it, so a damaged or hostile

    class SizedEntry

# A file prepared for someone to download, such as a whole account or one person's cards.
# Subclasses decide what goes into the archive; this class handles building it, notifying
# the requester, and expiring the download link.
class Export < ApplicationRecord
  DOWNLOAD_WINDOW = 1.day

  belongs_to :account, default: -> { Current.account }
  belongs_to :user

  has_one_attached :file, dependent: :purge_later

  enum :status, { pending: "pending", processing: "processing", completed: "completed", failed: "failed" }

  scope :expired, -> { where(expires_at: ..Time.current) }

  class << self
    def cleanup
      expired.destroy_all
    end
  end

  def process_later
    Export::ProcessJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def process_now
    processing!

    ZipFile.create_for(file, filename: archive_filename) do |zip|
      write_archive(zip)
    end

    update!(status: :completed, completed_at: Time.current, expires_at: DOWNLOAD_WINDOW.from_now)
    ExportMailer.completed(self).deliver_later
  rescue StandardError => error
    Rails.error.report(error, handled: true, severity: :error)
    update!(status: :failed, expires_at: DOWNLOAD_WINDOW.from_now)
    ExportMailer.failed(self).deliver_later
  end

  def downloadable?
    completed? && file.attached? && expires_at.present? && expires_at.future?
  end

  # Lets ActiveStorage's redirect controller hand out the file to the person who asked for it.
  def accessible_to?(accessor)
    accessor == user && downloadable?
  end

  private
    def write_archive(zip)
      raise NotImplementedError, "Subclasses write their archive contents"
    end

    def archive_filename
      "#{archive_name}-#{Date.current.iso8601}.zip"
    end
end

Signup only creates accounts when `Account.accepting_signups?` allows it, which on a single-tenant self-hosted instance means only when no account exists yet. My import route would bypass that rule. class Account::ImportsController < ApplicationController
  disallow_account_scope

  before_action :ensure_accepting_accounts

  layout "public"

  def new
  end

  def create
    file = params[:file]

    if file.respond_to?(:tempfile) && file.original_filename.to_s.downcase.end_with?(".zip")
      import = Account::Import.create_from_upload!(identity: Current.identity, file: file)
      import.process_later

      redirect_to session_menu_path(script_name: nil), notice: "Thanks! We'll email you when your account is ready to use."
    else
      redirect_to new_account_import_path(script_name: nil), alert: "Choose the .zip file you exported from Fizzy."
    end
  end

  private
    # Importing creates an account, so it follows the same rules as signing up for one.
    def ensure_accepting_accounts
      unless Account.accepting_signups?
        redirect_to session_menu_path(script_name: nil), alert: "This Fizzy isn't accepting new accounts."
      end
    end
end

cd /app && cat > docs/data-export-and-import.md <<'EOF'
# Exporting and importing accounts

Fizzy can export an account as a single `.zip` file and import that file as a new account, on the same instance or another one (self-hosted or SaaS).

## Exporting

- **The whole account (admins):** open *Account Settings* and choose **Export account**. The export runs in the background, and an email with a download link arrives when it's ready.
- **The cards you can see (anyone):** open your profile and choose **Export my cards**. You get the published cards on boards you have access to, with their comments and files.

Download links work for one day after the export is ready. After that they stop working, and the export files are removed by a recurring task (`Export.cleanup`). Only the person who asked for an export can download it.

### Account archive

```
manifest.json                   format name and version, when it was exported, the account name
records/<table>.ndjson          one JSON object per row, one file per table, in the order they're restored
files/<blob id>/<filename>      the bytes of every uploaded file, keyed by the blob ID used in the records
```

Records are written before files, so an archive can be restored in a single pass.

### Cards archive

```
manifest.json                   format name and version, the account and person it was made for, card count
cards/<number>.json             one card: its details, its comments, and the files attached to it and to its comments
files/<blob id>/<filename>      the files, referenced by `path` from the card JSON
```

## Importing

1. Sign in, then open **Import an account from a Fizzy export** from the account menu, or go to `/account/imports/new`.
2. Choose the account's `.zip` file and submit. The upload is stored, and the import runs in the background.
3. When it finishes, you get an email with a link to the new account. If it can't be completed, you get an email saying why.

What an import does:

- Creates a new account with its own ID, and restores its boards, columns, cards, comments, steps, tags, reactions, pins, watches, events, notifications, webhooks, and files.
- Makes the person doing the import the owner. If the file contains them (matched by email), their existing record is used.
- Adds the other people in the file as members. Anyone not yet on the instance gets an identity for their email address, and is unverified until they sign in.
- Keeps mentions and file references in comments working, pointing at the imported records.
- Rebuilds search, and recalculates storage usage.

An import that can't be completed leaves nothing behind. Its rows, files, search entries, and newly created identities are removed, and the uploaded file is deleted.

On a single-tenant instance, importing is only allowed while the instance has no accounts, the same rule that applies to signing up.

### Not included

These aren't part of an export, and aren't restored on import:

- Sign-in codes, sessions, passkeys, access tokens, join codes, and push subscriptions
- Saved filters
- Account cancellation state and the storage ledger (rebuilt from the files)
- The search index (rebuilt from the cards and comments)

## Storage and limits

Exports and imports use the instance's configured Active Storage service, so they work with local disk and S3 (see `config/storage.yml`). Archives are written and read as streams, so large accounts don't need to fit in memory or on local disk. Files are copied straight to storage on import, and each one is checked against the checksum recorded for it.

Recurring tasks keep this tidy:

- `Export.cleanup` (hourly) removes exports whose download window has passed.
- `Account::Import.cleanup_stale` (hourly) rolls back imports that stopped part way and haven't moved for a day.
EOF

class Account::DataTransfer::IdentifierMap
  def initialize(seed)
    @seed = [ ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.base36_to_hex(seed) ].pack("H*")
  end

  def map(id)
    digest = Digest::SHA256.digest(@seed + [ ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.base36_to_hex(id) ].pack("H*"))
    ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.hex_to_base36(digest.byteslice(0, 16).unpack1("H*"))

  # Rich text references people, attachments and other records by a signed global ID. The signature
  # belongs to the instance that exported it, so we read the ID (without verifying it), map it, and
  # sign it again with this instance's key. Returns nil when the reference can't be understood.
  def map_sgid(sgid)
    payload = sgid.rpartition("--").first
    global_id = GlobalID.parse(JSON.parse(Base64.decode64(payload)).dig("_rails", "data").split("?").first)

    mapped = "gid://#{GlobalID.app}/#{global_id.model_name}/#{map(global_id.model_id)}"

  end

  end

      end
    end
  end

  end

messages.content:
I've implemented account and cards export and import. The full non-system suite passes (1523 runs, 0 failures, against a 1444-run baseline), and rubocop and brakeman are clean on the new code.

## What it does

- **Whole-account export (admins):** an "Export account" button in Account Settings. The zip is built in the background and attached through ActiveStorage, so local disk and S3 both work. The requester gets an email with the link.
- **Cards export (anyone):** an "Export my cards" button on your own profile. It contains one JSON file per card that you can see, with its comments, plus every picture and file attached to the card or its comments.
- **Download links:** they work for one day, and only for the person who asked. An hourly task removes expired exports.
- **Import:** `/account/imports/new` takes a zip and creates a new account with boards, cards, comments, files, and people. The importer becomes the owner. An email reports success, or failure with the reason.
- **Failed imports leave nothing behind:** rows, files, search entries, and any identities created are removed. The uploaded zip is deleted in every case, and an hourly task rolls back imports that stop partway.

## Design choices

- **Archive format:** `manifest.json`, then one NDJSON file per table, then the raw files under `files/<blob id>/`. Records come before files, so import is a single pass.
- **Streaming both ways:** the writer streams through ZipKit. The reader is my own, because `rubyzip` is only a test-time dependency here. It checks each entry's CRC and size, so a truncated or damaged archive fails loudly.
- **IDs:** each import derives new IDs from the exported ID and a per-import seed. The same file can be imported twice, even into the same database.
- **Visibility:** the account has no members until the very end, so nobody sees a half-restored account.
- **Rich text:** mention and attachment references are re-signed with the local key, so they still resolve after import.
- **Single-tenant rule:** importing follows the same rule as signup, so a self-hosted instance that already has an account refuses an import.

## Pre-existing code I fixed

- `ZipFile::Writer` never saw the bytes ZipKit wrote, so the stored size and checksum were wrong. Now they're tracked correctly.
- Rich-text export wrote the rendered HTML, so every import added another wrapper. It now writes the stored text.
- The original `Account::DataTransfer` skeleton had no serialization. I filled it in.

## Known gaps and things to decide

- **Saved filters aren't exported.** They have join tables with no account column. I left them out rather than rush them.
- **Imported members stay unverified, and nothing verifies them automatically.** The existing verification step is only reached through the join-code flow, so imported people won't receive notification emails until something verifies them. This needs a product decision.
- **Untested paths:** S3 is exercised only with stubs, not a real bucket. MySQL isn't tested, and `db/schema.rb` is hand-written to match the SQLite migration. System (browser) tests weren't run.
- **Limits:** there's no upload size limit, no progress reporting, and no zip-bomb ratio check beyond each file's declared size.

Documentation is in `docs/data-export-and-import.md`. The working tree is uncommitted.
